scope: Senior holistic RedCap architecture smell audit across product shape, workflow guarantees, truth sources, knowledge and evidence lifecycle, package surface, human status surfaces, retrieval pressure, old/new transition residue, and Prism governance.

prism_review.normalization_note: Both reviewers used their raw blockers field for major findings or known human release decisions. Parsed Prism payloads preserve those raw notes as provider_reported_blockers and normalize current-task blockers to an empty list because neither reviewer reported a P0 stop condition for completing the audit itself.

domain_reviews.summary: Root-level structure and entry files remain cognitively broad for a future public product. The physical consolidation itself is already tracked by RASG-017, while related product-surface findings were linked or registered separately.
Knowledge lifecycle has strong gateway, cold archive, Forge, and LLM-wiki-lite controls. Remaining issues are lower-priority enforcement and archive-size observations, not new P1 blockers.
Receipt and evidence machinery is strong, but evidence/report roots remain physically scattered and prism/runs remains a local volume hotspot.
No new P1/P2 architecture smell was found in Layer B FSM, change intake, promise ledger, closeout runtime, or receipt aggregation for this audit scope.
Host entry duplication and incomplete runtime host-adapter shape remain visible, but are linked to existing host lifecycle and runtime productization requirements rather than new P1s.
The package candidate surface still mixes public runtime contract and maintainer-only governance tools. This was promoted to new pre-release debt RASG-020.
Human-facing CLI, Feishu, progress, and report summaries still leak internal workflow vocabulary as the main narrative. This was promoted to new pre-release debt RASG-019.
Indexing and gateway controls mitigate token pressure, but prism/runs and references remain notable pressure points if future tooling bypasses the intended lookup routes.

Layer A loom residue, historical migration manifests, root SKILL.md positioning, and runtime wrapper alpha boundaries remain visible old/new transition residue. Most are linked to existing RASG lines or candidate pool.
Prism is functional but resource-limited outcomes appear often enough to require a degradation-frequency status mechanism. This was promoted to new pre-release debt RASG-021.

findings.title: Root-level information architecture remains too broad for product release
findings.acceptance_boundary: RASG-017 must inventory root asset roots, define the target parent model, map consumers, and plan aliases before any physical migration.

findings.title: Root Markdown and host entry files are still easy to confuse
findings.acceptance_boundary: Do not create a duplicate requirement unless RASG-017 implementation fails to cover root entry classification or RASG-012 fails to cover host-entry drift detection.

findings.title: Human-facing output still uses internal workflow jargon as the main story
findings.acceptance_boundary: Human-facing CLI, Feishu, progress, and report summaries must explain problem/action/result/next-step first; mechanism names can remain only as secondary evidence.

findings.title: Public runtime package surface and maintainer governance surface are still mixed
findings.acceptance_boundary: Release readiness must classify public runtime contract, host adapters, documentation, maintainer tools, private-local files, and excluded files before public publish.

findings.title: Prism resource-limited outcomes need visible degradation tracking
findings.acceptance_boundary: A status surface must report recent full-quorum versus resource-limited frequency and warn when degradation crosses a threshold.

findings.title: Evidence and report assets remain physically scattered and prism/runs remains a local volume hotspot
findings.acceptance_boundary: RASG-017 should include the evidence parent model; RASG-008/RASG-014 continue to govern lifecycle, rotation, and archive safety.

findings.title: Runtime facade, host-adapter coverage, and root SKILL positioning still need clearer alpha/product boundaries
findings.acceptance_boundary: Do not treat wrapper-based runtime as fully split public API unless release handoff explicitly says alpha-wrapper contract.

findings.title: Knowledge gateway is strong but still mostly advisory without host-level read interception
findings.acceptance_boundary: Keep as a candidate until a host can enforce file-read policy broadly enough without breaking legitimate archaeology.

findings.title: Historical migration manifests and Layer A loom residue still create old/new transition noise
findings.acceptance_boundary: Only physically move or rename after consumer checks, aliases, and Prism review; RASG-017 may absorb part of this.

findings.title: Prism synthesis faithfulness and archive legacy bridge need later machine hardening
findings.acceptance_boundary: Track as Prism v0.3 hardening candidates; do not block RASG-018 because both are below the P1 threshold selected for this audit.

findings.title: Read-only sandbox status surfaces may degrade because some diagnostics expect writable temporary state
findings.acceptance_boundary: Candidate for later host-limited hardening; not a current release blocker unless release target includes read-only reviewer environments.

findings.title: Cold archive size and stale report age remain watch items
findings.acceptance_boundary: No new backlog item unless cold archive or report age crosses an explicit policy threshold.

must_not_claim: Do not claim RASG-018 fixes the P1 issues it discovered.
Do not claim all historical smells are repaired; RASG-017, RASG-019, RASG-020, and RASG-021 remain planned.
Do not physically move, delete, publish, or publicly migrate assets based only on this audit artifact.
